levelIntro.data-tutorial: Swipe right to keep a record, left to trash it. Or tap the buttons. Follow the hand first.
levelIntro.data-l1: Keep good records and trash broken ones. Not sure? Open the rulebook. Beat the clock!
levelIntro.data-l2: New move: swipe up or tap Fix to correct small slips. Only trash what can't be saved.
levelIntro.data-l3: Tap the bars that are errors. Unusual isn't wrong, so leave possible values alone.

tutorialHint.keep: Every field filled? Swipe right to keep.
tutorialHint.trash: Something's missing. Swipe left to trash.

toast.wrongTrashValid: That record was fine. Keep it!
toast.wrongTrashFixable: Rule 4: fix it, don't trash it.

answer: This one's a {action}. Rule {rule} decides it.
timeUp: Time's up! Let's see how you did.

outlier.instruction: Tap only the bars that are impossible. Big but possible values are outliers, not errors. Then tap Done.
outlier.missed: You missed an error. Look for impossible values.
outlier.wrongTap: Unusual, but possible. Rule 5: keep it.

automate.question: Which rule would you turn into code first?

options.dupes: Trash any household ID that's already appeared
options.big-households: Trash any household with over 12 people
options.typos: Trash every record with a typo

automate.right: Spot on. A repeated ID is always an error, so code can trash it safely.
automate.wrong: Good thinking, but that bins good data. Unusual isn't wrong, and typos can be fixed. Duplicates are safest.

result.heading0: Messy data is tricky. Have another go!

learned: You cleaned {count} records by hand. Write a rule once as code, and a pipeline (an automatic chain of steps) cleans millions.
